answer: Make each agent publish a real book before it can trade. First, it registers an ISBN in its own name and prints its public key in the front matter. Second, the national catalog confirms the title, and the record grows like a willow: one trunk, one name, one key. Third, peers spot-check a random page against the catalog copy. Forging 1,000 identities means writing 1,000 books at $125 per ISBN plus months of work, over $125,000 before one trade. A sybil swarm is like a relic dealer selling the same 'original' a thousand times, and the lantern of the catalog check ends the sale.
